verdict.status: Qualified representative river-system identity supported; exact reach-name application held.
verdict.identity_confidence: Moderate-to-high at regional representative-system scale; exact named-river extent and headwater boundaries are unresolved.
verdict.scope: The selected two-fragment mainstem group is geographically consistent with the Sarysu system, including separately named upstream river components and a seasonally active lower continuation. This is a system-level identification, not a claim that every selected line part is named Sarysu.
verdict.korean_note: No direct Korean naming source was acquired; no Korean transliteration or product display name is cleared.

geometry_integrity.canonical_hash_serialization: UTF-8 compact JSON with sorted object keys and unescaped Unicode; group geometry hash is the fragmentIndex-ordered list of complete geometry objects.

fragment_observations.geographic_observation: The eastern start lies near 73.61°E,48.51°N. The complete upper path initially bends south of 48.5°N, then crosses westward near 48.3–48.7°N before curving southwest to the fragment junction near 67.99°E,47.38°N. This is consistent with the regional Sarysu upper-system pattern, including a separately named eastern headwater; no exact headwater name boundary was determined.

The entire second fragment continues from the first junction south-southwest, near 67°E, through the lower valley to the endorheic endpoint near 66.94°E,45.14°N. The full lower path agrees at regional scale with the mapped southern basin arm; its terminal coordinate is not a proven named mouth, lake-membership point or contemporary shoreline.

spatial_identity_check.method: Read both complete decoded MultiLineStrings and all ordered source-ID lists, verify counts and canonical hashes, and inspect the full-group plot against the complete regional basin maps and geographic narrative. This is full-path qualitative comparison, not centroid proximity matching or an exact cartographic overlay.
observations: The full east–west upper path, southwest bend and long southward lower path jointly fit the Sarysu basin geometry. Both fragments were assessed; the southern part was not inferred from the upper fragment alone.

The source basin maps include tributary catchments and a boundary much wider than the selected line group. This finding does not give the Sarysu name to that entire polygon, every tributary, or an unselected network.

The thematic maps show a named basin and numbered field sites, rather than names attached to every reach. Their evidence supports regional representative identity while leaving precise headwater naming unresolved.
The shared fragment junction is a baseline packaging boundary. It is not established as a hydronym boundary.

The study distinguishes a 761 km named-river convention from a longer hydrological path exceeding 950 km through an upstream component. The inventory length 909.906 km is therefore not used as an exact named-river match.

limits: This is a fresh evidence reconstruction, not restoration of a previous verdict.
The current live deployment and equality to it were not checked.
The underlying HydroRIVERS shapefile was not acquired, so metadata reach order does not establish original per-reach coordinate equality.
No naming-register decision or formal naming-effective date was acquired.
The two research publications share leading authors; they are distinct documents but not wholly independent naming authorities.
Regional maps are thematic and generalized; they do not prove an exact named mouth, present-day water boundary, or individual headwater transition.
The unsuccessful 2022 yearbook was excluded, and its contents or search snippets were not used as acquired evidence.
No topology, geometry, terminal snapping or source-ID repairs were made.

endorheic_terminal_scope.endpoint_semantics: Retained baseline metadata, not independent proof of a named mouth.
endorheic_terminal_scope.source_context: The research sources describe lower-system losses and episodic delivery to the terminal-lake region; the 2024 government announcement supplies a dated managed-flood connection.
